chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from Shu'ayb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Every thing from which wealth flows upon you, so purify it (pay Zakat), and every thing you inherit or is gifted to you, so face the next year with it.'

key_terms.فَاسْتَقْبِلْ بِهِ: So face it (with the coming year)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat on inherited or gifted wealth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle that any wealth accumulating through one's efforts requires purification via Zakat, while inherited or gifted assets are subject to the standard rule of holding for a full lunar year (hawl) before the obligation arises. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between wealth acquired through active gain versus passive acquisition, ensuring the spiritual and material purity of one's assets. The hadith underscores the transformative nature of Zakat, linking financial obligation to spiritual cleansing as a comprehensive system of economic justice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Shuayb who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every thing from the wealth which flows upon you, so purify it (pay Zakāt), and everything you inherit or is gifted to you, so face the next year with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad all from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Aban from Shu’ayb who has said the following:
“Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Whatever you gain by means of assets, pay Zakat thereof and whatever you receive as inheritance or gift, pay Zakat thereof after a year passes.’”
